what_this_is: the registry of candidate showcases admitted to this repository, and the conditions each is admitted under. tools/verify_claims.py reads it; a showcase that is not listed here fails no_bulk_candidate_dump_in_paper_tree exactly as any other candidate file does
why_this_exists: The prohibition it relaxes is not decoration. A bulk dump of thousands of candidate records is unreviewable, and its presence in a paper tree invites the affinity and efficacy claims contracts/GEOAUDIT_PAPER_SCOPE.json forbids. Both objections are about volume and about claims, and neither applies to a small, field-complete, individually audited set admitted for one stated purpose.

This began as one hard-coded path for the ESR1 decomposability showcase. A second showcase then had to be admitted, and hard-coding a second path would have made the third one easy and the tenth one invisible. A registry is harder to widen than a list of paths in code: adding a showcase is a diff to a contract that states what it is admitted for, what it may not claim, and how many records it may hold.

The premise the whole exception rests on is that this repository is private, so nothing in it is a publication and no prior art is created against a composition claim in an absolute-novelty jurisdiction. AGENTS.md states that hazard and it is the only irreversible one here. Every showcase must declare repository_is_private, and repository_visibility_confirmed_at records when that declaration was last checked against the remote rather than believed.

global.why_a_total_cap: per-showcase caps do not bound the tree. Ten showcases of twelve records each is a dump assembled one contract diff at a time, and the total is what the reviewability argument is actually about

why_each_declaration.clinical_grade: no number in this repository supports a therapeutic decision, and a candidate record is the file most likely to be read as though it does
why_each_declaration.comparative_claim: the scope contract forbids comparing method classes, and the measured pLM-NN deficit contradicts any such claim regardless
why_each_declaration.efficacy_or_affinity_claim: nothing here measures binding. A structure, a pharmacophore and an alert profile are computed properties of a molecule and not evidence that it works
why_each_declaration.repository_is_private: the exception's premise. If this repository becomes public, every showcase in it becomes a publication and the filing order AGENTS.md requires has to be settled first

global.why_field_completeness_is_the_condition: completeness is the whole basis on which the exception was granted, so it is enforced field by field rather than trusted. A record without its bond graph is a name, a record without its stereochemistry is ambiguous as a chemical object, and a record without its structural audit is a proposal with no statement of what is wrong with it
global.why_the_default_can_be_overridden: the list above is the shape of a finished showcase. An input file carries the same molecules at an earlier stage -- identifiers and the audit verdict, no derived chemistry -- and demanding a bond graph of it would either fail honest files or push their authors to fabricate the field. An entry may therefore state its own required_fields_on_every_record, but it must also state why_its_own_fields, and the audit keys below are required of every role because the reason to withdraw a record does not depend on which file it sits in
global.why_those_four: a candidate that is cheap to make and cheap to assay is not a candidate if it degrades on the shelf, carries a known toxicophore, is cleared before it reaches anything, or is a mixture of stereoisomers one of which was never intended. Each of the four is a reason to withdraw a record, and a showcase that cannot state them has not audited anything

why_the_showcase_list_is_empty: It held two ESR1 entries until 2026-08-03. They were withdrawn because the premise the whole exception rests on -- 'this repository is private, so nothing in it is a publication' -- is false and was false when it was written.

repository_visibility_confirmed_at recorded 'checked 2026-07-31, result: private' and named the command that established it. That command returns isPrivate false. GitHub's public events timeline holds this repository's CreateEvent at 2026-07-05T04:49:13Z and continuous public pushes through 2026-08-03, including two on 2026-07-31 itself, and that timeline does not carry events from private repositories. The repository has been public for its entire existence.

The consequence was not hypothetical. Six ESR1 candidate compositions -- isomeric SMILES, bond-graph images, and their pairing with a pocket decomposition, which the filing order names as the sensitive combination -- were disclosed worldwide from 2026-07-30T13:23Z until they were withdrawn. In jurisdictions with no grace period that disclosure stands and no git operation reverses it. The material now lives in the private companion repository and the exposure window is recorded in its FILING_ORDER.md.

Every control in this registry worked. The prohibition was structural, the completeness gate read every field, the caps held, and the declarations were required and present. All of it sat on one hand-written observation of a mutable external fact, and that observation was wrong. The field now recording visibility is generated by tools/record_repository_visibility.py, and verify_claims.py withholds the exception unless the generated result is 'private'.

To re-admit a showcase: make the repository private, run tools/record_repository_visibility.py, confirm the generated result reads 'private', and settle the filing order first. Editing this file by hand is what caused the disclosure.
how_to_add_one: Append an entry here naming the path, the schema, the cap and what the showcase is admitted for. 'admitted_for' has to name a property the showcase demonstrates; 'a set of candidates for target X' is not one, because it does not say what a reader learns.

If the showcase carries a structure figure -- a cryo-EM map, a deposited experimental structure, a docked pose -- list its field in additional_required_fields together with the field naming its provenance, so a figure cannot appear without the accession or the method that produced it.
Run make verify. The gate fails closed on every clause: a missing field, a record over the cap, a total over the global cap, an undeclared claim, or a path not in this registry.

repository_visibility_confirmed_at.why_generated: a hand-written 'result: private' in this field was false on the day it was written and six candidate compositions were published under it. The premise of an irreversible exception is established by running the command, never by recording that it was run

public_timeline.what_it_means: GitHub's public events timeline does not carry events from private repositories, so any event here is positive evidence the repository was public at that event's timestamp. An empty timeline is only weak evidence of privacy, because events also age out of the window

repository_visibility_confirmed_at.why_that_result: api is_private=False; public timeline holds 203 event(s) from 2026-07-05T04:40:02Z to 2026-08-03T01:20:40Z. Either signal alone is enough to withhold the exception
